==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=actual|:inh|enm:real|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|real}}, from {{der|en|fro|reel}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|reālis||actual}}, from {{der|en|la|rēs||matter, thing}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*reh₁ís||wealth, goods}}. {{doublet|en|realis}}. In modern times, likely strengthened by or conflated with the use of the prefix ''re-'', analyzable as {{m|en|re-}} + {{m|en|-al}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|rēl, rēəl}} 
* {{IPA|en|/ɹiːl/|/ˈɹiː.əl/|/ɹɪl/|[ɹɪɫ]|a=RP,AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪj(ə)l/|[ɹɪj(ə)ɫ]|a=SSB}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-real.ogg|a=SSB|IPA=/ɹɪjəl/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɹi.əl/|/ɹil/|/ɹɪl/|[ɹɪɫ]|a=US,CA}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-real.ogg|a=US|IPA=/ˈɹi.əl/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɾil/|/ɾi.əl/|a=Scotland}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɾiːl/|/ɾiː.əl/|a=Wales}}
* {{IPA|en|/rɪjəl/|a=Indic}}

* {{homophones|en|reel}} {{q|some accents}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːəl|iːl|s1=2|s2=1}}

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|er,more}}

# {{senseid|en|genuine, not nominal, not merely in name}} [[true|True]], [[genuine]], not merely [[nominal]] or [[apparent]].
#: {{ux|en|City hall has its place, but this pub is the '''real''' heart of the town.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-29|volume=407|issue=8842|page=55| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/21580191-edward-snowdens-odyssey-leaves-america-nonplussed-and-its-allies-dismayed-russia-china Travels and travails]| passage=Even without hovering drones, a lurking assassin, a thumping score and a denouement, the real-life story of Edward Snowden, a rogue spy on the run, could be straight out of the cinema. But, as with Hollywood, the subplots and exotic locations may distract from the '''real''' message: America’s discomfort and its foes’ glee.}}
# {{senseid|en|genuine, not fake, not counterfeit}} [[genuine|Genuine]], not [[artificial]], [[counterfeit]], or [[fake]].
#: {{ux|en|This is '''real''' leather.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|title=A better waterworks|date=2013-06-01| volume=407| issue=8838| page=5 (Technology Quarterly)| url=http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578526-medical-technology-artificial-kidneys-are-getting-closer-becoming-clinical| passage=An artificial kidney these days still means a refrigerator-sized dialysis machine. Such devices mimic the way '''real''' kidneys cleanse blood and eject impurities and surplus water as urine.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625180618/http://www.economist.com:80/news/technology-quarterly/21578526-medical-technology-artificial-kidneys-are-getting-closer-becoming-clinical|archivedate=25 June 2017}}
# {{senseid|en|genuine, unfeigned, sincere}} [[genuine|Genuine]], [[unfeigned]], [[sincere]].
#: {{ux|en|These are '''real''' tears!}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=9|passage=Whose perfection farr excell’d Hers in all real dignitie|year=1873}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman| volume=189| issue=2| page=27| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google The tao of tech]| passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you{{...}}"share the things you love with the world" and so on. But the '''real''' way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.}}
# {{senseid|en|existing, not fictitious, not imaginary}} [[actually|Actually]] [[be]]ing, [[exist]]ing, or [[occur]]ring; not [[fictitious]] or [[imaginary]].
#: ''a description of '''real''' life''
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=7|passage=I waked, and found / Before mine eyes all '''real''', as the dream / Had lively shadowed.|year=1873}}
# {{senseid|en|real-life, in-the-flesh}} That has [[objective]], [[physical]] [[existence]].
#: {{ux|en|No one has ever seen a '''real''' unicorn.}}
# {{senseid|en|adjusted for inflation, in economics}} {{lb|en|economics}} Having been adjusted to remove the effects of [[inflation]]; measured in [[purchasing power]] {{qualifier|contrast ''[[nominal]]''}}.
#: {{ux|en|My dad calculated my family's '''real''' consumption per month.}}
#: {{ux|en|What is the '''real''' GNP of this polity?}}
# {{senseid|en|neoclassical rather than Keynesian, in economics}} {{lb|en|economics}} Relating to the result of the actions of rational agents; relating to neoclassical economic models as opposed to Keynesian models.
# {{senseid|en|rational or of a limit related to rationality, in mathematics}} {{lb|en|mathematics|of a number}} Being either a [[rational]] number, or the limit of a convergent infinite sequence of rational numbers: being one of a set of numbers with a one-to-one correspondence to the points on a line.
# {{senseid|en|relating to immovable tangible property}} {{lb|en|legal}} Relating to immovable tangible property.
#: {{ux|en|[['''real''' estate]]; [['''real''' property]]}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Cunning|passage=Many are perfect in men's humours that are not greatly capable of the '''real''' part of business.}}
# {{senseid|en|absolute, complete, utter}} [[absolute|Absolute]], [[complete]], [[utter]].
#: {{ux|en|This is a '''real''' problem.}}
# {{senseid|en|successful via genuineness}} {{lb|en|slang}} {{non-gloss|Signifying [[meritorious]] [[qualities]] or [[actions]], especially with regard to [[genuineness]], [[groundedness]], and true success rather than [[poser#English:_poseur|poser]] imitations of success.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm [[keep it real|keeping it '''real''']].}}
## [[firm|Firm]] through [[directness]], readiness to confront.
##: {{ux|en| yo, Imma be '''real''' with u... don't ever text me again}}

=====Synonyms=====

* {{antsense|that has physical existence}} {{l|en|fictitious}}, {{l|en|imaginary}}, {{l|en|made-up}}, {{l|en|pretend}} {{qualifier|informal}}
* {{antsense|relating to numbers with a one-to-one correspondence to the points on a line}} {{l|en|imaginary}}

{{ety|en|id=Spanish currency}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}

** {{rhymes|en|ɑːl|s=2}}

===Etymology 3===
{{ety|en|id=Portuguese currency|:bor|pt:real<id:royal>}}
[[File:Novas cedulas real thumb11-450x309.jpg|thumb|Brazilian '''real''' banknotes]]
From {{bor|en|pt|real|t=royal|id=royal}}, from {{der|en|la|rēgālis||regal; royal}}. {{doublet|en|ariary|regal|riyal|royal}}.

====Pronunciation====

* {{enPR|rāäl'|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/ɹeɪˈɑl/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-real (Spanish).wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɑːl|ɑl|s=2}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun|reis|réis|s}}

# {{senseid|en|Portuguese currency}} A unit of [[currency]] used in [[Portugal]] and its colonies from 1430 until 1911, and in [[Brazil]] from 1790 until 1942.
#: {{syn|en|rei}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A coin worth one real.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|reais|s}}

# {{senseid|en|Brazilian currency}} A unit of [[currency]] used in [[Brazil]] since 1994. Symbol: {{l|en|R$}}.
#: {{meronyms|en|centavo}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2011|author=Perry Anderson|title=Lula's Brazil|journal=London Review of Books|section=33.VII
|passage=Within weeks of this bombshell, an aide to the brother of the chairman of the PT, José Genoino, was arrested boarding a flight with 200,000 '''reais''' in a suitcase and $100,000 in his underpants.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A coin worth one real.
